detailed_description: Radar Chart Generator creates an editable ECharts radar chart for comparing multiple dimensions across one or more data series. Start from the sample budget-versus-actual data, add or remove indicators, set each indicator name and max value, add or remove series, edit series values in the table, and choose a chart title. The settings panel includes four color themes, polygon or circle radar shape, fill opacity, and a legend toggle. You can import a simple comma-separated CSV file where the first row contains indicator names and later rows contain series values, then download the rendered chart as PNG or SVG.
usage_steps: Load the sample data or edit the default indicator and series tables directly.
Use Add Indicator to create another radar axis and set its max value.
Use Add Series to compare another group of values across the same indicators.
Optionally import a simple CSV file with a first label column and indicator columns.
Choose a color theme, polygon or circle shape, fill opacity, and legend visibility.
Download the rendered radar chart as PNG or SVG when the preview looks right.
usage_examples: Compare budget and actual performance across sales, administration, technology, support, development, and marketing.
Create a product-feature scorecard with one series per competitor or release option.
Import a small CSV export from a spreadsheet and download the radar chart for a report.
Switch between polygon and circle shapes to see which chart reads better for a presentation.

faqs.question: What CSV format works best?
faqs.answer: Use a simple comma-separated file. The first row should contain a blank or series label column followed by indicator names, and each later row should contain a series name followed by numeric values.

faqs.question: Can I export the chart?
faqs.answer: Yes. The visible chart can be downloaded as PNG or SVG.

faqs.question: Does it support complex spreadsheet CSV features?
faqs.answer: No. The importer is a lightweight comma splitter and is best for simple plain-text data.

faqs.question: Can I edit line styles individually?
faqs.answer: No. The current controls cover theme, shape, fill opacity, legend visibility, indicators, series names, and values.
